## Executive Summary

The UK insurance sector is one of Insights360's highest-potential verticals — and the regulatory clock is running. The FCA's Consumer Duty enforcement has moved from implementation to active prosecution: six investigations are open (January 2026 Enforcement Watch), two targeting insurance firms specifically, with confirmed total FCA fines of £124m+ in 2025. Which? filed a formal super-complaint on 23 September 2025 targeting home and travel insurers for poor claims outcomes. The FCA named claims handling as its 2024/25 insurance focus area in December 2024 and published findings in July 2025. This is not a future risk — it is a current enforcement reality.

**The ICP cut is confirmed and sharpened.** Large composite insurers (Aviva, AXA, Direct Line, LV=, Ageas, RSA, Allianz UK) are OUT — enterprise QA incumbents are already deployed. Lloyd's wholesale market is OUT — no consumer contact centre, limited Consumer Duty scope. The real opportunity sits in three tightly-defined sub-segments: **insurance brokers** (10–150 seats, ~5,000–8,000 FCA-authorised intermediaries), **MGAs** (5–50 seats, 249 MGAA members, ~350 total), and **InsurTechs** (10–80 seats, cloud-native CCaaS stacks compatible with Insights360's architecture). A fourth window sits in **mid-size personal lines insurers and large national brokers** (50–150 seats) for firms not yet committed to enterprise QA tools.

**The pricing window is widening.** EvaluAgent confirmed a price increase in April 2026 to **£25/seat/month** for Auto-QA (up from £20 — a 25% increase). Insights360's Starter plan sits at £4.99/seat. The gap is now **5x** at the floor, and Insights360's no-seat-minimum and no-annual-commitment remain unique differentiators. Scorebuddy continues opaque pricing with AI scoring caps (500/month Accelerate, 1,000/month Elite) that make full-coverage economics unpredictable.

**Five archetypes define the market.** All are reachable with current product. The priority sequence: (1) Enforcement-Adjacent Brokers — firms under FCA voluntary requirements or post-enforcement remediation, for whom board-level evidence is non-negotiable now; (2) PE-Acquired Brokers — post-acquisition integration cycles create compliance standardisation demand across consolidator portfolios; (3) Governance-Pressured MGAs — capacity provider governance audits and the MGAA Consumer Duty controls framework; (4) Scaling InsurTechs — growing into full FCA Consumer Duty scope with cloud CCaaS stacks; (5) Mid-Size Personal Lines — board report pressure at 50–150 seats where enterprise tools are over-priced.

**Critical product constraint for [campaign agent]:** Audio playback in-browser with transcript synchronisation is NOT live (Theme 4, Sprints 12–14). Risk flags surface today; audio access via Insights360 does not. [content agent] and [outreach agent] must not write this angle until Theme 4 ships.

## MODULE 1 — Market & Company Landscape

### UK Insurance Market Size

The UK insurance market is the third-largest in the world. For campaign sizing purposes:

- **General insurance GWP:** ~£80bn in 2024 (IBISWorld), growing to an estimated £85.4bn in 2025. The Bank of England's Solvency II return for 2023 shows £123.6bn non-life GWP from UK-regulated insurers — this broader figure includes London Market reinsurance accepted and is not a retail-consumer comparison. The IBISWorld £80bn figure is the cleaner retail general insurance anchor. `strong` (multiple source triangulation)
- **Insurance intermediary sector revenue:** £26.2bn in 2024 (FCA RMAR non-investment insurance distribution revenue, published November 2025) — up 6.6% from £24.6bn in 2023. This is commission and fees earned by FCA-regulated intermediaries distributing insurance. `strong` (FCA primary data)
- **UK insurance broker market (firms):** ~1,770 businesses (IBISWorld 2026 estimate), ~70,851 employees. `moderate`
- **FCA-regulated intermediary population:** ~12,000 firms complete at least one element of the FCA Retail Mediation Activities Return (RMAR) — covering all retail intermediary types including insurance distribution. `strong` (FCA RMAR 2024)
- **MGA sector:** 249 MGAA member firms (MGAA Annual Report 2025), ~350 total UK MGAs including non-MGAA members. MGAs collectively manage 10%+ of UK GI premiums. `strong` (MGAA primary data)
- **Motor insurance GWP:** £22.3bn in 2024 (Milliman analysis of Solvency II returns), up from £18.4bn in 2023. ABI confirms motor claims hit a record £11.7bn in 2024. `strong`
- **Home insurance (personal property):** £10.3bn personal property GWP (Bank of England Solvency II, 2023). Average buildings + contents premium: £391 (Q2 2025, ABI). `strong`
- **FOS insurance complaints 2024/25:** 45,606 new insurance cases; 38% uphold rate (above all-products average of 34%). Most complained-about product: motor insurance with 14,082 cases. 31% of insurance cases concern a declined claim (up from 24%). `strong` (FOS Annual Report 2024/25, published 2 July 2025)

### Sub-Segment Breakdown

| Sub-segment | UK count (est.) | Seat range (typical) | ICP fit | Primary buying trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Large composite insurers (Aviva, AXA, Direct Line, LV=, Ageas, RSA, Allianz UK) | ~15 major brands | 500+ | OUT | Enterprise QA incumbents already deployed |
| Mid-size personal lines insurers (Hastings Direct, esure, Domestic & General) | ~30–50 | 100–500 | LOW | Upper seat count above ICP; procurement resembles mid-enterprise |
| Commercial/specialist lines (Hiscox, Chubb UK, QBE, Beazley) | ~50–100 | 5–100 | MEDIUM | Consumer Duty + claims compliance; broker-support lines in sweet spot |
| Insurance brokers (regional, national, non-Lloyd's) | ~5,000–8,000 FCA-authorised | 10–150 | **HIGH** | Consumer Duty board evidence; complaints root cause; M&A integration |
| MGAs (MGAA member and wider) | ~350 total (249 MGAA) | 5–50 | **HIGH** | Capacity provider governance; ~130 Consumer Duty controls to evidence |
| InsurTechs (FCA-regulated digital insurers/distributors) | ~100–200 | 10–80 | **HIGH** | Scaling into FCA Consumer Duty scope; cloud CCaaS stacks compatible |
| Lloyd's market (wholesale/specialty syndicates) | ~100 syndicates | N/A | OUT | No consumer contact centre; limited Consumer Duty scope |

**ICP prioritisation rationale:** The broker sub-segment is the highest volume opportunity — thousands of FCA-authorised firms in the 10–150 seat range, manual QA near-universal, and Consumer Duty obligations identical to large insurers but with far fewer resources. MGAs are fewer but have acute governance pressure from capacity providers. InsurTechs are smaller per account but faster procurement and often on compatible cloud CCaaS infrastructure. `strong` on this prioritisation — directly derived from FCA intermediary count, MGAA data, and product seat-band fit.

### Regulatory Bodies

| Body | Role | Relevance to campaign |
|---|---|---|
| **FCA** (Financial Conduct Authority) | Conduct regulator. Authorises and supervises all insurance intermediaries (brokers, MGAs, InsurTechs) under ICOBS, Consumer Duty, PROD 4, DISP. Primary day-to-day regulator. | Primary enforcement trigger. Consumer Duty evidence, complaints handling, claims disclosure obligations are all FCA-enforced. |
| **PRA** (Prudential Regulation Authority) | Prudential supervision of ~1,500 insurers (carriers). Not relevant to brokers or MGAs (FCA-only regulated). | Not a direct campaign driver. Mention only for carriers in the commercial/specialist sub-segment. |
| **FOS** (Financial Ombudsman Service) | Independent adjudication of consumer complaints. Binding on firms up to £430,000 per complaint. 45,606 insurance cases in 2024/25, 38% uphold rate. | The FOS complaint data is publicly available per-firm. High-complaint-rate firms are identifiable — this is a prospecting signal (see Module 4). |
| **ICO** (Information Commissioner's Office) | UK GDPR compliance. Relevant to call recording, consent management, AI analytics use. FCA/ICO joint guidance on AI and data expected Q1 2026. | Data residency and UK GDPR compliance are purchase-qualification questions. Insights360: UK/EU data residency, ISO 27001 group-level. |
| **Lloyd's of London** | Additional framework for Lloyd's syndicates and coverholders. | Relevant only for MGA prospects operating as Lloyd's coverholders (e.g., DUAL, CFC, Atrium). |

### Buying Triggers

Ranked by urgency intensity observed in the sector as of May 2026:

1. **FCA enforcement event in firm's group** — FCA voluntary requirements (VREQs), skilled persons review (s.166), or direct enforcement action. Board-level evidence demand becomes non-negotiable immediately. `strong` — documented in at least 5 named firms (see Module 4)
2. **Which? super-complaint response cycle** — Filed 23 September 2025. FCA responded December 2025. Industry-wide scrutiny of claims outcomes is elevated. `strong` — confirmed from FCA response document
3. **Annual Consumer Duty board report cycle** — Boards sign off by 31 July each year. Purchase intent concentrates in the 6–8 weeks preceding the deadline (typically May–July). A repeating annual window. `strong` — FCA PS22/9 confirmed
4. **Post-acquisition integration** — New PE owner or trade acquirer mandates compliance standardisation. Typical QA tooling review occurs 6–18 months post-deal. `strong` — documented across 10+ named firms (Module 4)
5. **Capacity provider governance audit** (MGAs) — Lloyd's, Zurich, AXA, RSA capacity providers scrutinising MGA governance controls including contact centre quality. `strong` — DUAL ERICCA framework documented
6. **FOS complaint rate spike** — FCA publishes firm-level bi-annual data. Above-average complaint rate (≥5/1,000 policies) creates board pressure and FOS scrutiny. `moderate` — FCA data confirmed, trigger inference is `moderate`
7. **Contact centre headcount growth** — QA coverage per FTE falls as volume grows. Manual sampling becomes statistically meaningless above ~30 seats. `strong` — structural arithmetic confirmed by ContactBabel data
8. **Renewal cycle on enterprise QA tool** — Buyer reviewing NICE/Verint/EvaluAgent renewal. 6-month pre-renewal pipeline window. `moderate` — no firm-level data on current contract cycles

### Volume Metrics Relevant to Insights360

- **ICOBS call recording reality:** There is no FCA mandatory call recording requirement for general insurance brokers under ICOBS. However, SYSC 9 record-keeping obligations and DISP complaints handling requirements make recorded calls the practical standard for disputes — near-universal in practice. `strong` (FCA guidance, ICOBS sourcebook, 2017 RWA compliance advisory confirmed)
- **The gap Insights360 fills:** The recordings exist. The systematic analysis — QA scoring, compliance rule verification, outcome monitoring — does not. This is the "95% invisible" opportunity.
- **ContactBabel 2024:** Insurance and housing sectors show the highest reliance on telephony-handled interactions of any UK vertical market sector. `strong`
- **FOS complaint rates as targeting proxy:** The FCA publishes bi-annual firm-level complaints data at fca.org.uk. BISL/Budget Insurance: 9.56 complaints per 1,000 policies (H2 2025 — above sector average). This data is free and public. [outreach agent] can build a prospect filter from it.

## MODULE 2 — Competitive Landscape

### Direct Competitors

#### EvaluAgent
- **URL:** evaluagent.com
- **Current pricing (UK, confirmed April 2026):** Auto-QA & Improvement from **£25/user/month** *(confirmed price increase from £20 — 25% rise)*; Conversation Intelligence from **£40/user/month**. Annual contract norms. `strong` — read directly from live pricing page updated 2026-04-14
- **Positioning:** "The #1 AutoQA Platform for Contact Centres." Sweet spot: 50–500 agents. UK-headquartered, ISO 27001, G2 Best UK Sellers 2025 and 2026.
- **Insurance-sector moves (confirmed 2026-05-18):** `strong`
  - Named insurance customer: **1st Central** (UK motor insurer, ~4m customers). Results: 95% reduction in QA planning time, FCR improvement ~1.3pp "worth hundreds of thousands of pounds annually."
  - Named customers: **ManyPets** (pet insurance, FCA-regulated), **Vitality** (health/life insurance), **Capital on Tap** (FCA credit).
  - **xVulnerability feature** — proprietary metric scanning 100% of conversations for vulnerability signals (literacy/numeracy difficulties, financial difficulty, changing circumstances). Explicitly positioned against FCA Consumer Duty vulnerability obligations. This is a named product differentiator.

## MODULE 3 — Persona Intelligence (Archetypes)

Five archetypes. Each is a sector + size + situation combination grounded in named firm evidence.

---

### Archetype 1: "The Enforcement-Adjacent Broker"

**Organisation profile:** UK regional or specialist insurance broker, 15–80 contact centre seats. FCA-regulated under ICOBS and Consumer Duty. Currently under FCA voluntary requirements (VREQs), recovering from a group-level enforcement action, or exposed to an active FCA investigation. Board-level Consumer Duty evidence demand is immediate and non-negotiable. Examples: BISL/Budget Insurance, Brightside, Hughes Insurance Services, One Call Insurance.

**Dominant pain:** Cannot evidence consumer outcomes to the FCA's required standard. Manual QA covers 2–5% of calls. The annual Consumer Duty board report was signed off on a sample that the compliance team knows is indefensible. The next reporting cycle is approaching and the evidence base hasn't improved. `strong` — FCA Enforcement Watch Issue 1, Jan 2026; FCA PS22/9 board reporting requirement

**Buyer roles (with seniority):**
- **Operations Director / Head of Customer Operations** — *Director level.* Budget holder. Needs defensible evidence for board and FCA. Signs the purchase.
- **Head of Compliance / Compliance Manager** — *Senior Manager.* FCA liaison. Owns the Consumer Duty evidence pack. Primary internal advocate.
- **QA Manager** — *Middle Management.* Day-to-day champion. Runs the manual reviews. Knows the coverage gap from the inside.

**Opening angle:** "Six Consumer Duty investigations are open at the FCA. Two target insurance firms specifically. The FCA's question is not 'do you have a QA process?' — it's 'can you prove outcomes for 100% of customer interactions?' At 2–5% sampling, the answer is no."

**Deal economics:**
- Typical seat count: 20–50 seats
- Professional plan (£7.99/seat): £1,918–£4,794/year
- Total Year 1 (inc. setup £1,280 + config review £640): ~£3,838–£6,714
- Sales cycle: 4–8 weeks (urgency is acute; procurement layers are thin at this firm size)
- Budget owner: Operations Director or Compliance budget line

---

### Archetype 2: "The PE-Acquired Broker"

**Organisation profile:** UK insurance broker, 20–100 contact centre seats, 0–18 months post-acquisition by an active consolidator (Jensten/Bain Capital, PIB Group, Clear Group, Ardonagh Advisory, JMG/GTCR). New PE or trade owner has stated technology investment and operational standardisation as priorities. Compliance harmonisation is a known active workstream. Examples: Jensten Group and all recent acquisitions, PIB acquired entities, JMG/GTCR portfolio, Clear Group acquisitions, Ardonagh acquisitions.

**Dominant pain:** Pre-acquisition QA processes don't meet group compliance standards. The new group COO or technology team is conducting an operational audit. Manual QA is the most visible and easiest-to-remediate infrastructure gap. Timing is 6–18 months post-deal — the initial integration (HR, payroll, IT systems) is complete, and operational standardisation (QA, compliance monitoring) is the next phase. `strong` — documented across 10+ named acquisitions (Module 4); PE integration pattern is a known buying trigger

**Buyer roles (with seniority):**
- **Group Operations Director / Group COO** (acquirer side) — *Director/C-suite.* Mandates the standardisation. May purchase group-wide rather than entity by entity.
- **Branch/Entity Operations Director** (acquired entity) — *Director.* Implementing the mandate from new parent. Needs to show progress.
- **Group Compliance Manager** (acquirer side) — *Senior Manager.* Initiating the compliance audit that surfaces the gap.

**Opening angle:** "Group-level Consumer Duty compliance standards apply across the portfolio from day one. Newly acquired entities need to meet them. We're working with several post-acquisition integration programmes in the UK broker sector right now. Insights360 can be live within weeks — no annual commitment."

**Deal economics:**
- Typical seat count: 30–60 seats per entity
- Multi-entity opportunity: consolidators with 10–20 acquired entities = portfolio roll-out discussion
- Professional plan: £2,877–£5,753/year per entity
- Sales cycle: 6–12 weeks (group IT review required; procurement involves new parent's sign-off process)

---

### Archetype 3: "The Governance-Pressured MGA"

**Organisation profile:** UK FCA-authorised MGA, MGAA member, 5–50 contact centre seats. Consumer-facing operations: renewals, claims, broker support. Under direct pressure from capacity providers (Lloyd's, Zurich, AXA, RSA) to evidence governance controls including contact centre quality. Actively working through Consumer Duty controls framework — the DUAL ERICCA exercise (20 open controls as of June 2025) is the documented archetype. Examples: DUAL UK, Prestige Underwriting, CFC Underwriting, Iprism, KGM Underwriting.

**Dominant pain:** Capacity provider is asking for evidence of claims handling quality and consumer outcomes monitoring. The MGA's compliance team can demonstrate process — QA scorecards exist — but cannot produce call-level evidence across 100% of interactions. The gap is most acute in claims calls, where the FCA's July 2025 thematic findings apply directly. `strong` — DUAL ERICCA framework documented; FCA July 2025 claims handling review confirmed

**Buyer roles (with seniority):**
- **COO / Head of Operations** — *Director.* Budget holder at smaller MGAs.
- **Compliance Manager** — *Senior Manager.* Building the governance evidence pack for capacity provider audit.
- **Claims Manager** — *Middle Management.* Operational champion for claims call quality. Day-to-day user.

**Opening angle:** "The FCA published claims handling findings in July 2025: 'We only saw a few examples where firms demonstrated claim settlements being comprehensively monitored, tested, assessed, and understood.' When your capacity provider asks for outcomes evidence from claims calls, what do you produce?"

**Deal economics:**
- Typical seat count: 10–30 seats
- At Professional plan (£7.99/seat): £958–£2,877/year + setup
- The no-seat-minimum is decisive: EvaluAgent's economic floor (25–50 seats) puts it out of reach for most MGAs. Insights360 is viable at 5 seats.
- Sales cycle: 6–10 weeks

---

### Archetype 4: "The Scaling InsurTech"

**Organisation profile:** UK-based FCA-regulated InsurTech or digital insurer, 10–80 contact centre seats. Cloud-native CCaaS infrastructure — 8x8, Five9, RingCentral, Talkdesk — all in Insights360's architecture compatibility list. Growing fast; typically launched consumer-facing products in the prior 12–24 months, bringing full FCA Consumer Duty obligations into scope. QA infrastructure lags growth velocity. Examples: Zego, Marshmallow, ManyPets, Inshur, Urban Jungle.

**Dominant pain:** Consumer Duty compliance for phone interactions is being built while the contact centre scales. The compliance team is focused on product governance and policy design; call quality monitoring is the unmanned gap. FCA vulnerability obligations apply from day one of consumer-facing operations. `strong` — Consumer Duty regulatory fact; confirmed for Zego (new consumer product Jan 2025), Marshmallow (expansion), ManyPets (new UK carrier April 2024)

**Buyer roles (with seniority):**
- **Head of Operations / VP Operations** — *VP/Head-of.* Budget holder. Fewer procurement layers than traditional insurers.
- **Head of Compliance / Chief Compliance Officer** — *Director.* Owns the Consumer Duty obligation. Advocates internally.
- **Head of Customer Support** — *Middle Management.* Day-to-day operational champion. Runs the contact centre.

**Opening angle:** "You launched consumer-facing products. FCA Consumer Duty applies from day one. As call volume grows, the gap between what your QA team can manually review and what your FCA obligations require grows with it. Build the compliance infrastructure once, correctly, at this scale — not at Series B with 10× the call volume."

**Deal economics:**
- Typical seat count: 15–60 seats (growing)
- At Professional plan: £1,438–£5,753/year + setup; seat count increases year-over-year
- Procurement cycle faster than traditional insurance: InsurTechs have internal agility. But data residency and ISO 27001 still required — both on Insights360's product spec sheet.
- Sales cycle: 3–6 weeks

---

### Archetype 5: "The Mid-Size Personal Lines Insurer or Large National Broker"

**Organisation profile:** Mid-size UK personal lines insurer or large national broker, 50–150 contact centre seats. Not yet committed to enterprise QA (no NICE/Verint contract in place, or approaching renewal). Consumer Duty board reporting pressure is acute because the contact centre is the primary consumer outcome data source at this scale. Examples: Swinton/Atlanta Group (though under FCA restrictions), Domestic & General, Coversure franchise network.

**Dominant pain:** Enterprise QA tools (NICE, Verint) were over-priced; mid-market tools (EvaluAgent at £25/seat, now requiring ~£15,000–£45,000/year for this seat band plus annual commitment) carry contracts the operations team resists. The board report evidence gap is identical to the smaller archetypes but at greater scale — the compliance team is producing a board report on 5% of millions of calls. `strong` — FCA board reporting requirement; pricing arithmetic confirmed

**Buyer roles (with seniority):**
- **Contact Centre Director** — *Director.* Budget holder.
- **Chief Compliance Officer / Head of Compliance** — *Director.* Annual board report is their deliverable.
- **Head of QA** — *Senior Manager.* Operational champion.

**Opening angle:** "The annual Consumer Duty board report requires you to evidence outcomes for your customer population — not a sample. If your QA team is sampling 5% of calls at 100 seats, the board is signing off on 5% of the evidence. Insights360 scores 100% of calls at £4.99–£9.99/seat, no annual commitment."

**Deal economics:**
- Typical seat count: 50–150 seats
- At Professional plan (£7.99/seat): £4,794–£14,382/year + setup
- May require a formal business case for procurement sign-off at this scale
- Sales cycle: 6–12 weeks

## MODULE 5 — Pain Points by Archetype

Pain points ranked by acuity within each archetype. All carry confidence tags.

---

### Archetype 1: Enforcement-Adjacent Broker

1. **FCA board-level evidence demand for Consumer Duty compliance.** The FCA's Enforcement Watch Issue 1 (January 2026) disclosed six open investigations into Consumer Duty fair value breaches — two targeting insurance firms. Firms under voluntary requirements must demonstrate remediation to the FCA's satisfaction. Manual QA covering 2–5% of calls cannot constitute outcomes evidence. `strong` — FCA Enforcement Watch #1, Jan 2026; FCA PS22/9

2. **Complaints root cause analysis without call-level data.** The FCA reviewed 40 firms' complaints root cause analysis in 2024 and found firms "were capturing complaints data but it was not granular enough to understand outcomes for different customer groups." Without call-level data, complaints analysis rests on complaint text alone. `strong` — FCA Complaints and Root Cause Analysis, December 2024 (primary FCA publication)

3. **Vulnerable customer identification gaps.** FCA Consumer Duty cross-cutting rule on vulnerable customers requires identification and accommodation. Vulnerability signals (distress, confusion, financial difficulty) are in the call audio. Manual QA at 2–5% coverage misses 95% of them. `strong` — FCA Consumer Duty focus areas 2024/25; FCA Consumer Support Outcome thematic March 2025

4. **Audit trail for FCA enquiries.** When FCA supervisors request evidence of outcomes monitoring, firms under VREQs must produce it promptly. An ad-hoc collection of manual QA spreadsheets is not an audit trail. `strong` — FCA enforcement process; SYSC 9 record-keeping requirements

5. **Claims disclosure compliance verification.** FCA's 2024/25 specific focus for general insurance: claims handling arrangements. Every unreviewed claims call is an unverified disclosure. `strong` — FCA Consumer Duty Focus Areas 2024/25; FCA claims handling report July 2025

---

### Archetype 2: PE-Acquired Broker

1. **Compliance standards harmonisation across the acquired entity.** New PE owner's group compliance standards require evidence of systematic call quality monitoring. Pre-acquisition manual QA process fails the group standard on day one. `strong` — documented across Jensten/Bain, PIB, Clear Group, Ardonagh integration patterns

2. **Demonstrating QA capability to new parent within the integration timeline.** PE owners typically expect operational improvements within 12–18 months. QA tooling is a visible, measurable, quickly-deployable improvement. `moderate` — inferred from PE investment cycle norms; no primary source for specific broker timelines

3. **Consumer Duty board report under new ownership.** The annual Consumer Duty board report deadline (31 July) does not pause for ownership changes. The new parent is signing off on the first board report — and the evidence base is a 2–5% sample. `strong` — FCA PS22/9 requirement is unchanged regardless of corporate restructuring

4. **ROI framing for PE parent.** PE owners evaluate operational investment on ROI. The QA reviewer cost arithmetic is stark: Insights360 Professional at 30 seats = £2,877/year; one UK contact centre QA reviewer = ~£28,000/year and reviews 2–5% of calls. `moderate` — pricing arithmetic confirmed; £28k reviewer salary estimate is reasonable but not directly sourced

5. **Speed to value.** PE integration timelines are defined and monitored. A QA tooling decision that takes 12 months to evaluate and implement does not serve the investment thesis. Weeks-to-live onboarding is a genuine differentiator. `strong` — product architecture confirmed; 3CX/OAK onboarding speed documented

---

### Archetype 3: Governance-Pressured MGA

1. **Capacity provider governance audit requiring call quality evidence.** Lloyd's, Zurich, AXA and RSA are scrutinising MGA governance controls including consumer outcomes monitoring. 2. **FCA claims handling thematic directly applicable to MGA operations.** FCA published July 2025: "We only saw a few examples where firms demonstrated claim settlements being comprehensively monitored, tested, assessed, and understood." MGAs handling direct consumer claims are in scope. `strong` — FCA primary publication July 2025

3. **MGA Consumer Duty control gaps — outcomes evidencing is the hardest category.** The MGAA/DUAL ERICCA framework's open controls cluster around outcomes monitoring and evidence production. 5. **Price proportionality — EvaluAgent's floor is above the MGA's seat count.** EvaluAgent at £25/seat × 15 seats = £4,500/year plus annual contract. ---

### Archetype 4: Scaling InsurTech

1. **Consumer Duty compliance gap from day one of consumer product launch.** FCA Consumer Duty applies to consumer-facing insurance products immediately on launch. 2. **QA infrastructure gaps as contact centre scales.** The manual QA reviewer model breaks down as call volume grows. A 30-seat InsurTech contact centre handling 10,000 calls/month at 5% manual review rate is sampling 500 calls. 4. **Data residency and regulatory compliance for AI analytics.** InsurTechs' investors and FCA authorisation both require UK data residency and ISO 27001 for any tool processing call recordings containing personal data. Insights360: UK/EU Vercel + AWS hosting, ISO 27001 group-level. This is a purchase-qualification gate, not just a differentiator. `strong` — Insights360 architecture confirmed; regulatory requirement confirmed

Weeks-to-live on 3CX or OAK; scoped timeline for other CCaaS platforms (Five9, 8x8, RingCentral). `strong` for 3CX/OAK; `moderate` for other platforms (scoped per-customer, timeline variable)

### Archetype 1: Enforcement-Adjacent Broker — Messaging

**Verbatim phrases from primary sources — for [content agent]/[outreach agent] use:**

FCA, Insurance Multi-Firm Review of Outcomes Monitoring (June 2024):
> *"Under the Consumer Duty firms must regularly assess, test, understand and evidence the outcomes their customers are receiving. Without this, it will be impossible for firms to know that they are meeting the requirements set out in the Duty."*

FCA, Complaints and Root Cause Analysis (December 2024):
> *"Some complaints data reports appeared to be prepared for operational discussions… rather than also considering how the data can help inform where the firm can improve customer outcomes."*

> *"It appeared that some firms saw the completion of RCA as the goal, rather than whether they needed to take further action to deliver good customer outcomes."*

Ridley & Co, FCA Consumer Duty Enforcement commentary:
> *"Having a Consumer Duty framework is no longer the question. Whether the framework produces outcomes with evidence is."*

> *"The FCA's question in 2026 is not whether you have one. It is whether your framework produces the outcomes it describes, whether you can prove it does and whether the proof survives scrutiny. That is an infrastructure question, not a policy question."*

Aveni, Consumer Duty Evidence Guide:
> *"The question every compliance officer and quality assurance leader should put to their current approach is not whether it looks like adequate evidence. It is whether it would hold up when an FCA supervisor looks closely at it. For many firms, that is a different question with a different answer."*

Max Contact, Consumer Duty guide for contact centre teams:
> *"When a complaint lands, you can't point to a sample. You need evidence that the specific interaction was handled correctly."*

### Archetype 2: PE-Acquired Broker — Messaging

**Verbatim phrases from primary sources:**

FCA, Insurance Outcomes Monitoring (June 2024):
> *"Some approaches were overly focused on processes being completed rather than on outcomes delivered."*

FCA, Complaints and Root Cause Analysis (December 2024):
> *"In some cases, firms appeared to be sending data to committees as a tick-box exercise rather than an opportunity to engage and drive change."*

Ridley & Co:
> *"The infrastructure that delivers on that policy includes: the data that measures whether the product actually delivers fair value, the governance process that reviews that data at a frequency that matches the risk, the escalation path when the data shows the product does not deliver fair value and the remediation process that follows. If any of those components is missing, the policy exists but the outcome does not."*

### Archetype 3: Governance-Pressured MGA — Messaging

**Verbatim phrases from primary sources:**

FCA, Home and Travel Claims Handling (July 2025):
> *"We only saw a few examples where firms demonstrated claim settlements being comprehensively monitored, tested, assessed, and understood."*

> *"We won't hesitate to act using our regulatory powers where we are concerned that firms are not upholding the requirements of the Consumer Duty or our regulatory requirements."*

FCA, Insurance Outcomes Monitoring (June 2024):
> *"Few firms were able to provide clear evidence of where the monitoring of outcomes had directly led to proactive action being taken to improve these outcomes, where necessary."*

> *"We saw little monitoring of whether overall good outcomes were being achieved in relation to claim settlements."*

> *"Poor practice: reliance on monitoring process completion rather than customer outcomes."*

Aveni:
> *"Unstructured notes that cannot be systematically reviewed. Many firms hold a significant amount of information about customer interactions in the form of adviser notes, contact centre records, and case management comments. The problem is that free-text, unstructured records cannot be systematically analysed."*

### Archetype 4: Scaling InsurTech — Messaging

**Verbatim phrases from primary sources:**

Voyc, Consumer Duty 2025/26 practitioner guide:
> *"Forward-looking compliance and operations leaders are already: linking QA insights directly to outcomes MI, stress-testing customer journeys for friction and vulnerability, and using conversation intelligence to surface evidence for board reports and audits."*

> *"The emphasis has shifted from 'doing' to 'demonstrating.' Firms that can show consistent, evidence-based outcomes will not only satisfy the regulator, they'll strengthen customer trust and competitive position."*

Max Contact:
> *"You will only know that your contact centre is complying with new FCA Consumer Duty rules by putting robust monitoring systems in place. That means measuring call centre performance and analysing complaints. It also involves regular agent reviews, audits of customer interactions and performance reviews."*

FCA, Inside Podcast (transcript):
> *"A key part of that is that firms understand and evidence the outcomes their consumers are receiving... without the information or the evidence it's not really possible for firms to know that they're meeting the requirements under the duty."*

### Archetype 5: Mid-Size Personal Lines / Large National Broker — Messaging

**Verbatim phrases from primary sources:**

FCA, Home and Travel Claims Handling (July 2025):
> *"[Firm A's] MI showed that key operational service level agreements were consistently outside of tolerance throughout 2024 and 70% of complaints about claims service had been upheld. This indicates significant issues that impact customer outcomes. Despite this, the firm reduced seasonal claims handling resources and had multiple vacancies in claims handling, further straining service delivery."*

Insurance Times, CII member survey on Consumer Duty board reporting (September 2025):
> *"'A lack of clarity in reporting undoubtedly tells a broader story of firms' abilities to achieve the goals intended with the FCA's Consumer Duty guidelines.'"*

> *"There was also an increase in firms reporting difficulty in showing the relationship between different data sets and manually entering data since 2024."*

Aveni:
> *"For Heads of Operations and QA Managers, consistency is also a training and resourcing challenge. Maintaining calibration across a team of assessors requires regular benchmarking sessions, shared case studies, and documented assessment criteria. Many firms run these exercises, but the inherent subjectivity of manual review limits how far calibration can go."*

CMS Law, FCA Consumer Duty Health-Check (April 2025):
> *"1LOD QA focussed on single/point in time interactions with customers rather than customers' experience across the whole duration of a journey: point-in-time checks limit ability to identify issues in the firm's overall treatment of customers, detect linked themes and root causes."*

## MODULE 7 — ICP Definition

### Ideal Company Profile (Firmographics)

- **Size:** 5–150 contact centre seats. Primary sweet spot: 10–80 seats (EvaluAgent's economic floor begins at 25–50 seats; below this, Insights360 has no credible direct competitor). Secondary zone: 80–150 seats (EvaluAgent viable but Insights360's no-lock-in and price advantage remain differentiating at this scale).
- **Sector:** UK FCA-regulated insurance sector — specifically: insurance brokers (ICOBS-regulated intermediaries), MGAs (FCA-authorised, MGAA membership is the quality signal), InsurTechs (FCA-regulated digital insurers and distributors), commercial and specialist lines insurers with small contact operations (5–100 seats). Commercial/specialist lines are MEDIUM priority — in seat range and regulatory profile, but procurement is more complex.
- **Sub-sector signals that improve ICP fit:** (a) Consumer Duty open or closed products in scope and board reporting due; (b) Contact centre handles consumer-facing interactions (renewals, new business, claims, complaints, broker support lines); (c) Not already locked into an enterprise QA vendor on a multi-year contract (NICE, Verint/Calabrio); (d) FCA RMAR reporter (i.e., classified as an insurance distribution firm by the FCA).
- **Geography:** UK primary. EU secondary — EIOPA IDD-regulated insurance intermediaries with UK-equivalent contact centre operations in Germany, Netherlands, France (Vercel Frankfurt fra1 = EU data residency; substitute IDD/GDPR framing for Consumer Duty in EU-facing materials). `moderate` on EU secondary urgency — no equivalent enforcement intensity to FCA Consumer Duty confirmed.
- **Regulatory exposure:** FCA Consumer Duty in force. FCA RMAR reporter. FOS-complaints-generating (consumer-facing, not wholesale/commercial-only).
- **Telephony stack:** Prioritise 3CX and OAK prospects (live connectors, turn-key onboarding, fastest time-to-value). Qualify Microsoft Teams, Cisco, Avaya, Mitel, 8x8, Five9, RingCentral early — compatible but requires per-customer scoping. Discovery call question: "What telephony platform are you on, and do you currently have call recordings stored centrally?"
- **Buying committee size:** 2–4 stakeholders. QA/Compliance champion + Operations Director (budget sign-off) + Finance/IT review (cost and data residency). NOT an enterprise RFP committee — if the process involves 6+ sign-offs and formal RFP, this is outside the typical Insights360 buying motion.
- **M&A status signal:** Firms 0–18 months post-acquisition by an active consolidator (PIB, Jensten/Bain, Clear, Ardonagh, JMG/GTCR, Gallagher) are HIGH priority regardless of other signals.

### Ideal Buyer Profile

- **Primary champion:** QA Manager / Head of QA, Compliance Manager / Head of Compliance, or Consumer Duty Lead — the person who knows the coverage gap from the inside and will champion the evaluation.
- **Secondary champion / budget holder:** Operations Director / Head of Operations — signs the purchase, needs defensible evidence for board and FCA.
- **Seniority range:** Champion is typically Middle Management to Senior Manager; budget holder is Director level. The two-stakeholder model (champion + budget holder) is the typical deal structure.
- **Role situation:** Currently running manual QA (sampling 2–5% of calls). Has either received internal pressure (board report challenge, compliance audit finding, new PE parent's expectations) or external pressure (FCA thematic review letter, capacity provider audit request, FOS elevated complaint rate, peer firm enforcement action).
- **What makes them ready to act now (ranked by urgency):**
  1. Active FCA enforcement action in their firm or group
  2. Annual Consumer Duty board report preparation (May–July window)
  3. Post-acquisition integration cycle with new PE parent mandate
  4. Capacity provider governance audit (MGAs)
  5. Recently launched consumer products (InsurTechs)
  6. FOS complaint rate spike (public metric, board-visible)
- **Channels that reach them:** LinkedIn (personalised outreach anchored in sector-specific regulatory content — name the FCA publication, not the generic "Consumer Duty" tag); email to direct role; FCA-adjacent compliance events (Huntswood roundtables); CCMA community; BIBA Conference (for Operations Directors).

### Disqualifiers

These are explicit exclusions. [campaign agent]'s `audience-intel` and `campaign-plan` both use this to prevent scope creep.

| Disqualifier | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Large composite insurers** — Aviva, AXA UK, Direct Line (post-acquisition by Aviva), LV=, Ageas, RSA, Allianz UK, Admiral (above 500 seats) | Enterprise QA tools already deployed or being procured (NICE, Verint). Wrong sales motion, wrong price point, wrong feature depth. | **OUT** |
| **Sub-5-seat operations** | £1,280 setup fee + per-seat fees + config review = economically non-viable for either party. | **OUT** |
| **250+ seat enterprise contact centres** | Enterprise QA tools (NICE, Verint) have features Insights360 deliberately does not (WFM integration, advanced routing, BYOK, agent desktop). Insights360 will lose a feature comparison at this scale. | **OUT** (unless a specific sub-department of ≤150 seats can be ringfenced) |
| **Real-time agent assist buyers** | Insights360 is post-call only, by architecture. If the buyer's primary stated need is live whisper coaching, call interruption, or real-time compliance alerts during the call, refer elsewhere. | **OUT** |
| **Pure call recording / voice retention buyers** | Insights360 does not record. It analyses recordings provided by the telephony platform. If the buying motion is "we need to start recording calls" rather than "we need to analyse our recordings," this is the wrong product. | **OUT** |
| **Marketing attribution / call tracking buyers** | Infinity, Mediahawk, ResponseTap prospects — different category. QA is secondary; marketing is primary. Refer elsewhere. | **OUT** |
| **Lloyd's wholesale-only firms** | No consumer-facing contact centre operations. Consumer Duty obligations limited for wholesale/commercial-only businesses. FCA and Lloyd's regulatory angle does not apply to the call centre use case. | **OUT** |
| **Non-FCA-regulated firms (Gibraltar-licensed, EEA passported)** | Consumer Duty angle does not apply. Weaker urgency. | **DEPRIORITISE** (not an absolute disqualifier if UK consumer operations and GDPR/IDD angles apply) |
| **Firms locked into multi-year enterprise QA contracts** | NICE or Verint/Calabrio on active contract with multiple years remaining. Competing mid-contract is not the right motion. | **DEFER** — add to 24-month pipeline, approach 6 months before renewal |
| **C-suite "digital transformation" narrative buyers** | The Insights360 buyer is operational, not strategic. If the entry point is a Chief Transformation Officer or CDO seeking an AI strategy statement, the product doesn't fit the buying motion. | **DEPRIORITISE** — re-route to operational champion |
| **Pure BPO/outsourced contact centres without direct FCA insurance obligations** | FCA Consumer Duty obligations rest on the FCA-regulated insurer or broker, not the BPO. The BPO may buy Insights360 on behalf of a regulated client — but the outbound motion should target the insurer/broker, not the BPO. | **DEPRIORITISE** as direct target; they may appear as implementation partners |

M&A status signal: Firms 0–18 months post-acquisition by an active consolidator (PIB, Jensten/Bain, Clear, Ardonagh, JMG/GTCR, Gallagher) are HIGH priority regardless of other signals.
idealBuyer: Primary champion: QA Manager / Head of QA, Compliance Manager / Head of Compliance, or Consumer Duty Lead — the person who knows the coverage gap from the inside and will champion the evaluation.
Secondary champion / budget holder: Operations Director / Head of Operations — signs the purchase, needs defensible evidence for board and FCA.
Seniority range: Champion is typically Middle Management to Senior Manager; budget holder is Director level. The two-stakeholder model (champion + budget holder) is the typical deal structure.

Role situation: Currently running manual QA (sampling 2–5% of calls). Has either received internal pressure (board report challenge, compliance audit finding, new PE parent's expectations) or external pressure (FCA thematic review letter, capacity provider audit request, FOS elevated complaint rate, peer firm enforcement action).

What makes them ready to act now (ranked by urgency): 1. Active FCA enforcement action in their firm or group 2. Annual Consumer Duty board report preparation (May–July window) 3. Post-acquisition integration cycle with new PE parent mandate 4. Capacity provider governance audit (MGAs) 5. Recently launched consumer products (InsurTechs) 6. FOS complaint rate spike (public metric, board-visible)

## MODULE 8 — Messaging & Positioning Framework

Per archetype: angles in priority order, language do/don't lists, sector-specific regulatory phrases, verbatim language from primary sources for [content agent]/[outreach agent] use.

Brand voice constraints active throughout (per brand-voice.md): lead with operational problem; quote prices openly; name the boundary; no transformation language; no empty SaaS adjectives.

---

### Archetype 1: Enforcement-Adjacent Broker — Messaging

**Angles (priority order):**

1. **FCA enforcement evidence** — "Six Consumer Duty investigations are open at the FCA. Two target insurance firms specifically. The FCA's compliance question is no longer 'do you have a QA process?' — it's 'can you prove outcomes for 100% of customer interactions?' At 2–5% sampling, you cannot."
2. **Consumer Duty board evidence** — "The board signs off annually on Consumer Duty evidence. A 5% sample covering the other 95% is not a defensible position when the FCA comes looking."
3. **Complaints root cause** — "When the FCA asks for call-level data behind a complaint pattern, what do you produce? If those calls weren't in the 2–5% reviewed, the answer is nothing."
4. **Price and risk** — "£4.99/seat/month vs the compliance risk of an FCA voluntary requirements notice. The arithmetic is straightforward."
5. **Speed** — "Weeks to live, not months. No annual commitment. If your FCA review is in three months, that timeline is achievable."

**Language DO (insurance enforcement register):**
- "outcomes monitoring," "FCA Consumer Duty evidence," "board report," "100% of calls," "root cause analysis," "audit trail," "call-level evidence," "risk flag," "compliance rate," "post-call," "voluntary requirements," "FCA enforcement," "claims handling arrangements," "vulnerable customer treatment," "fair value," "FOS uphold rate"

**Language DON'T (per brand-voice.md):**
- "AI-powered," "revolutionary," "real-time," "end-to-end," "seamlessly" (except Teams integration specifically), "unlock," "holistic," "world-class," "innovative," "disruptive," "cutting-edge," "leverage," "synergy"

**Regulatory phrases to acknowledge in copy (compliance register authenticity):**
- "Consumer Duty" / "Consumer Principle"
- "fair value assessment"
- "consumer outcomes" / "good consumer outcomes"
- "FCA Enforcement Watch"
- "voluntary requirements" (VREQs)
- "claims handling arrangements"
- "vulnerable customer treatment" / "characteristics of vulnerability"
- "outcomes monitoring"
- "ICOBS," "SYSC 9," "DISP"

**Verbatim phrases from primary sources — for [content agent]/[outreach agent] use:**

FCA, Insurance Multi-Firm Review of Outcomes Monitoring (June 2024):
> *"Under the Consumer Duty firms must regularly assess, test, understand and evidence the outcomes their customers are receiving. Without this, it will be impossible for firms to know that they are meeting the requirements set out in the Duty."*

FCA, Complaints and Root Cause Analysis (December 2024):
> *"Some complaints data reports appeared to be prepared for operational discussions… rather than also considering how the data can help inform where the firm can improve customer outcomes."*

> *"It appeared that some firms saw the completion of RCA as the goal, rather than whether they needed to take further action to deliver good customer outcomes."*

Ridley & Co, FCA Consumer Duty Enforcement commentary:
> *"Having a Consumer Duty framework is no longer the question. Whether the framework produces outcomes with evidence is."*

> *"The FCA's question in 2026 is not whether you have one. It is whether your framework produces the outcomes it describes, whether you can prove it does and whether the proof survives scrutiny. That is an infrastructure question, not a policy question."*

Aveni, Consumer Duty Evidence Guide:
> *"The question every compliance officer and quality assurance leader should put to their current approach is not whether it looks like adequate evidence. It is whether it would hold up when an FCA supervisor looks closely at it. For many firms, that is a different question with a different answer."*

Max Contact, Consumer Duty guide for contact centre teams:
> *"When a complaint lands, you can't point to a sample. You need evidence that the specific interaction was handled correctly."*

---

### Archetype 2: PE-Acquired Broker — Messaging

**Angles (priority order):**

1. **Integration speed** — "Group compliance standards apply from day one. Insights360 can be live within weeks — no annual commitment, no platform migration, no six-month implementation project."
2. **ROI framing for PE parent** — "£7.99/seat/month for automated QA across 100% of calls. One QA reviewer at £28,000/year covers 2–5% of calls. The arithmetic makes the case."
3. **Portfolio approach** — "If you're rolling out compliance infrastructure across multiple acquired entities, our no-seat-minimum model means you can start at the entity level, prove the value, and expand."
4. **Consumer Duty board report** — "The regulatory requirement doesn't pause for ownership changes. Your first board report under new ownership is the one to get right."
5. **No lock-in** — "If the group's integration strategy changes direction, there's no annual contract obligation to manage."

**Language DO:** "integration timeline," "group compliance standards," "portfolio-level deployment," "operational efficiency," "Consumer Duty board report," "no annual commitment," "100% of calls," "call-level evidence"

**Verbatim phrases from primary sources:**

FCA, Insurance Outcomes Monitoring (June 2024):
> *"Some approaches were overly focused on processes being completed rather than on outcomes delivered."*

FCA, Complaints and Root Cause Analysis (December 2024):
> *"In some cases, firms appeared to be sending data to committees as a tick-box exercise rather than an opportunity to engage and drive change."*

Ridley & Co:
> *"The infrastructure that delivers on that policy includes: the data that measures whether the product actually delivers fair value, the governance process that reviews that data at a frequency that matches the risk, the escalation path when the data shows the product does not deliver fair value and the remediation process that follows. If any of those components is missing, the policy exists but the outcome does not."*

---

### Archetype 3: Governance-Pressured MGA — Messaging

**Angles (priority order):**

1. **Capacity provider governance** — "When your capacity provider asks for evidence of claims handling quality from your contact centre, what do you produce?"
2. **FCA claims handling thematic** — "The FCA published claims handling findings in July 2025: 'We only saw a few examples where firms demonstrated claim settlements being comprehensively monitored, tested, assessed, and understood.' Are you one of those few?"
3. **Consumer Duty controls** — "The controls framework requires outcomes evidencing. Call analytics at 100% coverage is the shortest path from 'process compliance' to 'outcomes evidencing' — and it's the specific control gap capacity providers are now asking about."
4. **Price proportionality** — "At 15 seats, NICE isn't an option. EvaluAgent at £25/seat with an annual contract isn't proportionate. Insights360 at £7.99/seat, no minimum, no lock-in, is."
5. **Speed to capacity provider audit** — "The audit is in three months. We can have you live and scoring 100% of calls in weeks."

**Language DO:** "capacity provider governance," "claims outcomes," "Consumer Duty controls evidencing," "100% of calls," "outcomes monitoring," "FCA thematic review," "MGAA member," "demonstrating fair value," "30 open controls," "claims handling arrangements"

**Verbatim phrases from primary sources:**

FCA, Home and Travel Claims Handling (July 2025):
> *"We only saw a few examples where firms demonstrated claim settlements being comprehensively monitored, tested, assessed, and understood."*

> *"We won't hesitate to act using our regulatory powers where we are concerned that firms are not upholding the requirements of the Consumer Duty or our regulatory requirements."*

FCA, Insurance Outcomes Monitoring (June 2024):
> *"Few firms were able to provide clear evidence of where the monitoring of outcomes had directly led to proactive action being taken to improve these outcomes, where necessary."*

> *"We saw little monitoring of whether overall good outcomes were being achieved in relation to claim settlements."*

> *"Poor practice: reliance on monitoring process completion rather than customer outcomes."*

Aveni:
> *"Unstructured notes that cannot be systematically reviewed. Many firms hold a significant amount of information about customer interactions in the form of adviser notes, contact centre records, and case management comments. The problem is that free-text, unstructured records cannot be systematically analysed."*

---

### Archetype 4: Scaling InsurTech — Messaging

**Angles (priority order):**

1. **Build it right from the start** — "Consumer Duty applies from day one of consumer-facing operations. Build the compliance infrastructure once, correctly, at this scale — not at Series B with 10× the call volume and an FCA audit underway."
2. **Cloud CCaaS compatibility** — "We're built for the CCaaS platforms you're already on — 8x8, Five9, RingCentral. Your recordings, our analysis. No migration."
3. **Vulnerable customer at scale** — "As call volume grows, vulnerable customer signals get harder to catch manually. Sentiment analysis across 100% of calls surfaces what a 5% sample misses. FCA requires it. Your QA team can't deliver it without tooling."
4. **ISO 27001 and UK data residency** — "Your FCA authorisation and your investors both ask about data residency. UK and EU hosting is standard on our product spec sheet. Call data never leaves the UK-EU adequacy framework."
5. **Speed** — "Weeks to live. No annual commitment. If your call volume doubles next quarter, the pricing scales with it — not against you."

**Language DO:** "Consumer Duty from day one," "cloud-native," "post-call," "UK data residency," "ISO 27001," "sentiment analysis," "vulnerable customer signals," "no migration," "scale," "100% of calls"

**Language DON'T:** Same as above, plus: do NOT imply 8x8, Five9, or RingCentral are turn-key live connectors — they are "compatible but scoped per customer." Phrase: "We work with your existing CCaaS stack — we scope the connector during onboarding."

**Verbatim phrases from primary sources:**

Voyc, Consumer Duty 2025/26 practitioner guide:
> *"Forward-looking compliance and operations leaders are already: linking QA insights directly to outcomes MI, stress-testing customer journeys for friction and vulnerability, and using conversation intelligence to surface evidence for board reports and audits."*

> *"The emphasis has shifted from 'doing' to 'demonstrating.' Firms that can show consistent, evidence-based outcomes will not only satisfy the regulator, they'll strengthen customer trust and competitive position."*

Max Contact:
> *"You will only know that your contact centre is complying with new FCA Consumer Duty rules by putting robust monitoring systems in place. That means measuring call centre performance and analysing complaints. It also involves regular agent reviews, audits of customer interactions and performance reviews."*

FCA, Inside Podcast (transcript):
> *"A key part of that is that firms understand and evidence the outcomes their consumers are receiving... without the information or the evidence it's not really possible for firms to know that they're meeting the requirements under the duty."*

---

### Archetype 5: Mid-Size Personal Lines / Large National Broker — Messaging

**Angles (priority order):**

1. **Board report evidence gap** — "The annual Consumer Duty board report requires you to evidence outcomes for your customer population — not a sample. If your QA team is sampling 5% of calls at 100 seats, the board is signing off on 5% of the evidence. The FCA knows what good looks like, and a 5% sample isn't it."
2. **Price vs. enterprise tools** — "Enterprise tools built for 400+ seats don't fit a 100-seat operation. NICE CXone starts at £36/seat. EvaluAgent is now £25/seat with an annual contract. Insights360: £4.99–£9.99/seat, no minimum, no commitment."
3. **Complaints MI with call data** — "The FCA reviewed complaints root cause analysis at 40 firms. The consistent finding: not enough call-level data to find the pattern behind the complaint. Every call is categorised and scored. Every complaint has a call behind it — and you can find it."
4. **Claims disclosure compliance** — "The FCA's 2024/25 supervision focus is insurance claims handling. Were your agents completing every required disclosure on every claims call last month? We can tell you — for every call, not a sample."
5. **FOS complaint rate** — "The FCA publishes firm-level complaint rates bi-annually. High-rate firms are named publicly. Systematic QA surfaces the rule failures driving complaint patterns before they become FOS cases."

**Language DO:** Same as Archetype 1, plus: "FOS complaint rate," "firm-level data," "disclosure compliance," "ICOBS," "claims handling," "board sign-off," "100 seats"

**Verbatim phrases from primary sources:**

FCA, Home and Travel Claims Handling (July 2025):
> *"[Firm A's] MI showed that key operational service level agreements were consistently outside of tolerance throughout 2024 and 70% of complaints about claims service had been upheld. This indicates significant issues that impact customer outcomes. Despite this, the firm reduced seasonal claims handling resources and had multiple vacancies in claims handling, further straining service delivery."*

Insurance Times, CII member survey on Consumer Duty board reporting (September 2025):
> *"'A lack of clarity in reporting undoubtedly tells a broader story of firms' abilities to achieve the goals intended with the FCA's Consumer Duty guidelines.'"*

> *"There was also an increase in firms reporting difficulty in showing the relationship between different data sets and manually entering data since 2024."*

Aveni:
> *"For Heads of Operations and QA Managers, consistency is also a training and resourcing challenge. Maintaining calibration across a team of assessors requires regular benchmarking sessions, shared case studies, and documented assessment criteria. Many firms run these exercises, but the inherent subjectivity of manual review limits how far calibration can go."*

CMS Law, FCA Consumer Duty Health-Check (April 2025):
> *"1LOD QA focussed on single/point in time interactions with customers rather than customers' experience across the whole duration of a journey: point-in-time checks limit ability to identify issues in the firm's overall treatment of customers, detect linked themes and root causes."*

---

### EU Secondary Note

Germany, France, Netherlands: EIOPA Insurance Distribution Directive (IDD) creates analogous but distinct obligations — disclosure compliance, suitability documentation, complaints handling, and customer welfare obligations under IDD Article 17. No direct Consumer Duty equivalent; enforcement intensity is lower than FCA as of May 2026. `moderate` on EU urgency equivalence to UK — regulatory framework confirmed; enforcement intensity comparison is inferred.

- Substitute "FCA Consumer Duty" with "IDD compliance and GDPR-compliant call analytics"
- Lead with GDPR Article 5 (data minimisation, purpose limitation) — call analytics must have lawful basis; legitimate interest or consent required
- Substitute "FOS complaint rate" with "national ADR body" (Financial Ombudsman equivalents in DE/NL/FR)
- Data residency: Vercel Frankfurt fra1 = EU data residency, explicitly relevant and briefable

## Unknowns Flagged

1. **Calabrio/Verint corporate structure:** The wiki records these as a combined company post-Thoma Bravo acquisition (last verified 2026-05-15). A research agent flagged this may be incorrect — both entities have separate active websites. Before "combined company" language propagates into [campaign agent] campaign materials, [orchestrator] should verify current corporate structure. `[Flag to [orchestrator]]`

2. **Google Ads Transparency advertiser IDs** for EvaluAgent, Scorebuddy, Calabrio, NICE CXone: Not retrievable programmatically — the portal is a JavaScript SPA requiring browser-based lookup. Manual retrieval required. Method: adstransparency.google.com, search each name, click advertiser profile, read AR-prefixed ID from URL. `[Flag to [campaign agent] — manual browser task, ~2 min per vendor]`

3. **Mid-size insurer QA tooling status** (Hastings Direct, esure, Domestic & General): No intelligence found on current QA tools deployed at named mid-size personal lines insurers. This matters for competitive displacement framing. A follow-up pass targeting named mid-size insurer QA/compliance LinkedIn profiles would surface this. `[Flag to [orchestrator] for follow-up pass if Archetype 5 becomes priority]`

4. **Telephony stack distribution in the UK broker market:** No sourced data on which telephony platforms UK regional brokers most commonly run. This matters because 3CX and OAK are the only live connectors — if the broker market skews toward Avaya or Mitel, connector scoping will be a common early-conversation friction point. [the product owner] may be able to pull proxy data from C360 prospect history. `[Flag to [orchestrator]]`

5. **EvaluAgent insurance event presence:** No confirmed sponsorship or speaking slot at named UK insurance events (BIBA, Claims Technology Summit, Insurance Times events) in 2024–2025. Could not rule out entirely — event exhibitor lists are not comprehensively indexed. Monitor. `[Watch item]`

6. **One Call Insurance — current FCA compliance status:** The historical fine (circa 2018) predates current Consumer Duty. Whether One Call's remediation has been formally closed by the FCA or remains on record as an active concern is unknown without a direct FCA register check. `[Verify before using as Tier 1 target if regulatory sensitivity is a concern]`

7. **EU enforcement intensity:** The claim that EU Consumer Duty equivalent enforcement is less intense than FCA as of May 2026 is `moderate` — regulatory framework comparison confirmed; enforcement intensity comparison is inferred from FCA-specific enforcement data with no equivalent EU aggregate found.
